findings.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:40 — [P2, confidence 100] `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the complete configured feed import for every cache-miss embed request, so N concurrent requests for different URLs perform N feed downloads and N×M item imports despite the hourly scheduler, exhausting workers as the feed or request rate grows.

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — [P1, confidence 100] `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` assigns every pre-existing post the `raw_html` enum value, so the new `return raw` branch bypasses cooking for all historical posts instead of retaining the declared regular default.

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — [P1, confidence 100] `create_table :top_topics, force: true` changes an already-shipped migration to drop `top_topics` before recreating it whenever migrations are replayed, deleting all accumulated top-topic data.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — [P2][100] `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` commits the retry-suppression key before `fetch_http` succeeds, so a failed retrieval makes Sidekiq retries return success without importing the topic and leaves the visitor on the loading page.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — [P1][100] `open(url).read` performs the user-triggered remote import with neither a timeout nor a size limit, so a stalled or arbitrarily large source response holds the worker indefinitely and prevents the requested embed from completing.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — The unscoped replacement `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` removes the existing `--category` import interface, so established Disqus-import automation with `--category` exits on an unknown option instead of placing topics in the requested category; P1, confidence 100.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:19 — `creator = PostCreator.new(user, title: title, raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` persists attacker-controlled RSS or fetched-page HTML with validation bypassed and `Post#cook` returns it raw, so a publisher able to supply feed/article content executes persistent JavaScript in Discourse readers’ sessions [P1; confidence 100].

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:15 — `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any attacker-controlled origin that is a string prefix of the configured forum origin (for example `https://forum.example.co` for `https://forum.example.com`), so that origin can forge `discourse-resize` messages and force embedded pages to an attacker-chosen frame height [P3; confidence 75].

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:35 — P1 (confidence 100): `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once` replaces the newly added feed parsing/import unit with a mock, so malformed feed items, missing import users, URL fallback, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls all ship without behavioral verification despite the test suite reporting the polling path covered.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:40 — [P2, confidence 100] `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the complete configured feed import for every cache-miss embed request, so N concurrent requests for different URLs perform N feed downloads and N×M item imports despite the hourly scheduler, exhausting workers as the feed or request rate grows.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 38-41, `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` is called synchronously within `perform_retrieve` for every cache-miss embed request. Looking at the code: when `retrieved_recently?` returns false (cache miss), `perform_retrieve` is called, which then calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` if feed_polling_enabled. This means concurrent requests for different embed URLs that miss the throttle cache will each trigger a full feed poll operation. The throttle in `retrieved_recently?` is per-URL (using `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` as the key), so different URLs bypass each other's throttles. This is a real performance/scalability bug where N concurrent requests for N different URLs would trigger N feed downloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — [P1, confidence 100] `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` treats unnormalized URL spellings as distinct durable identities, so a request for `http://host:80/path` and the feed's `http://host/path` create separate topics for the same fetched resource and future embeds split their discussion.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real URL normalization issue. Looking at the diff, TopicEmbed.import() uses `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` to check for existing embeds, and stores the URL as-is without normalization. The same URL can have multiple equivalent representations (e.g., http://host:80/path vs http://host/path, trailing slashes, case differences in hostname). This means the same resource could create duplicate topics if accessed via different URL spellings. The code in topic_embed.rb lines 17-18 shows `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and later `TopicEmbed.create!(... embed_url: url ...)` without any URL canonicalization. This is a legitimate correctness bug that could cause duplicate topics for the same content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — [P2, confidence 100] `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` leaves ordinary relative links such as `href="chapter-2.html"` and `href="../assets/logo.png"` unconverted even though `absolutize_urls` promises to convert any relative URL, so imported feed articles contain links that resolve against the Discourse embed page instead of their source article.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the `absolutize_urls` method in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`. Looking at lines 56-70, the code only converts URLs that `start_with?('/')` - meaning absolute-path relative URLs like `/hello`. However, ordinary relative URLs like `chapter-2.html` or `../assets/logo.png` don't start with `/` and would be left unconverted. The method name `absolutize_urls` and comment 'Convert any relative URLs to absolute' suggest it should handle all relative URLs, but the implementation only handles root-relative ones. This would cause links in imported RSS content to break when viewed on Discourse.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — [P1, confidence 100] `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` assigns every pre-existing post the `raw_html` enum value, so the new `return raw` branch bypasses cooking for all historical posts instead of retaining the declared regular default.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug. In app/models/post.rb, the enum is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` which assigns :regular=1 and :raw_html=2. The migration sets `default: 1` which corresponds to :regular, not :raw_html. The cook method checks `if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` to return raw. Since existing posts get cook_method=1 (:regular), they will NOT bypass cooking - they'll continue through the normal cooking pipeline. The finding's claim that existing posts would bypass cooking is incorrect - the default of 1 means :regular which is the correct behavior. The finding misreads the enum ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — [P1, confidence 100] `create_table :top_topics, force: true` changes an already-shipped migration to drop `top_topics` before recreating it whenever migrations are replayed, deleting all accumulated top-topic data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb was modified to add 'force: true' to the create_table call. The diff shows '- create_table :top_topics do |t|' changed to '+ create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|'. Adding 'force: true' to an already-shipped migration means that if migrations are replayed (e.g., in a fresh database setup or certain deployment scenarios), it will drop the existing top_topics table before recreating it, potentially causing data loss. This is a real bug in the migration change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — [P2][100] `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` commits the retry-suppression key before `fetch_http` succeeds, so a failed retrieval makes Sidekiq retries return success without importing the topic and leaves the visitor on the loading page.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb, the `retrieved_recently?` method sets a Redis key with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and expires it for 60 seconds BEFORE `perform_retrieve` is called. The flow is: `retrieve` calls `retrieved_recently?` which sets the key, then calls `perform_retrieve`. If `perform_retrieve` fails (e.g., `fetch_http` throws an exception), the Redis key remains set for 60 seconds, preventing any retry attempts during that window. This means a failed retrieval will block subsequent attempts, leaving users on the loading page. The finding correctly identifies this race condition/error handling issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — [P1][100] `open(url).read` performs the user-triggered remote import with neither a timeout nor a size limit, so a stalled or arbitrarily large source response holds the worker indefinitely and prevents the requested embed from completing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` where `open(url).read` is called without any timeout or size limit. This is a user-triggered operation (via embed_url parameter in the controller) that fetches remote content. Without timeouts, a slow or malicious server could hold the worker indefinitely. Without size limits, an arbitrarily large response could exhaust memory. This is a real security/availability defect in the new code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in lib/tasks/disqus.thor, line 117 removes the `method_option :category` declaration (the line `method_option :category, aliases: '-c', desc: "The category to post in"` is deleted). Additionally, lines 144-148 show the removal of the category handling code that used `options[:category]` to find a category_id. This means existing automation scripts using `--category` or `-c` flags will fail because Thor will reject the unknown option. This is a breaking change to the CLI interface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — P1 (confidence 100): `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` makes the no-embed controller example fail because `EmbedController#best` now enqueues `:retrieve_topic` instead of constructing a `TopicRetriever`, so the test neither passes nor verifies the loading workflow it claims to cover.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the test fails because EmbedController#best enqueues :retrieve_topic instead of constructing TopicRetriever. Looking at the diff, embed_controller.rb line 14 shows `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` which is correct. However, the test in embed_controller_spec.rb lines 41-45 mocks TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever) and retriever.expects(:retrieve). The test also mocks TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed).returns(nil). The actual controller code calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic), not TopicRetriever.new directly. So the test IS incorrectly mocking - it expects TopicRetriever.new to be called but the controller actually enqueues a job. However, looking more carefully at the test setup with stubs/expects, the test would actually pass because TopicRetriever.expects(:new) would not fail if never called when using expects - it would only fail if called with wrong args. Actually, with Mocha, expects sets up an expectation that MUST be satisfied. So the finding appears correct that the test is broken. But wait - the test file is being added in this diff, so this is new code being added with a potentially broken test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:35 — P1 (confidence 100): `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once` replaces the newly added feed parsing/import unit with a mock, so malformed feed items, missing import users, URL fallback, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls all ship without behavioral verification despite the test suite reporting the polling path covered.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:35 uses `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once` which mocks out the actual `poll_feed` method. Looking at the diff, the `poll_feed` method in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb contains significant logic: parsing RSS feeds with SimpleRSS, iterating items, handling URL fallback (checking i.link vs i.id), unescaping HTML content, and calling TopicEmbed.import. The test only verifies that `poll_feed` gets called when settings are configured, but doesn't test the actual feed parsing logic. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for newly added nontrivial logic, though it's not a bug - the code may work correctly, it's just not tested at the unit level.
